groups.instruction: Each question gives some rules about which days of the week places open and people work. Take the rules to be completely true, work out what happens on every day, then pick the ONE statement the rules force to be so. Rules about a person always follow from the days already worked out for whatever they depend on.
groups.example: The pool opens only on Tuesday and Friday. Sam works on the days the pool is open. That fixes all seven days: the pool is open on Tuesday and Friday and shut otherwise, and Sam works on exactly those two days. So “Sam does not work on Monday” must be true, while “Sam works on Tuesday or Wednesday” is not something the rules force either way.

questions.stem: The leisure centre opens only on weekends (Saturday and Sunday). Which ONE of these must be true?
questions.explanation: The leisure centre opens only on weekends, so on Wednesday it is closed. That statement must be true.

options.text: The leisure centre is closed on Wednesday.
The leisure centre is open on Monday.
The leisure centre is open on Tuesday.
The leisure centre is closed on Sunday.
The leisure centre is closed on Saturday.

questions.stem: The cinema opens every day except Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Omar works on the days the cinema is open, except on Sunday. Which ONE of these cannot be true?
questions.explanation: On Tuesday, The cinema is closed, so Omar does not work. Every other statement is consistent with the rules; that one is not.

options.text: The cinema is open on Friday.
Omar works on Friday.
Omar does not work on Saturday.
Omar works on Tuesday.
The cinema is closed on Saturday.
